source_document.citation: Campello, M.; Cortes, G. S.; d'Almeida, F.; Kankanhalli, G. (2022). 'Exporting Uncertainty: The Impact of Brexit on Corporate America.' Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis, Vol. 57, No. 8 (December 2022), pp. 3178-3222.
source_document.verification_method: Verbatim text extracted via pdftotext; Table 2 (page 3200) and Table 8 (page 3208) visually rendered at 200 DPI and inspected to confirm row labels and cell entries.

user_prompt_corrections_upfront.user_claim: Table 8 column 1 has a row 'Macroeconomic: No.'
user_prompt_corrections_upfront.actual_situation: Table 8 has NO 'Macroeconomic' row at all. Its 'Controls' section lists only 'Firm' (= Yes for all 6 columns). The Macroeconomic row appears in Table 2, where it is 'Yes' for the linear-continuous specifications (cols 1, 4) and 'No' for the tercile and 10-K specifications (cols 2, 3, 5, 6). For Table 8, the macro-controls status is not separately reported in the table; it must be inferred from equation (14) and the surrounding text.
user_prompt_corrections_upfront.implication: Q3 of the prompt rests on a premise that is not in the table. The answer below addresses what the paper actually says, not the false premise.

Q1_estimation_equation.verbatim_paragraph_setting_up_equation_p: We compare differences in outcomes of interest between treated (HIGH_UK_EXPOSURE) and control (LOW_UK_EXPOSURE) firms. Differences over the 2016:Q3-Q4 period are taken relative to the same two quarters in the previous year (2015:Q3-Q4) in order to minimize the impact of seasonal effects. This is equivalent to estimating the following model:
Q1_estimation_equation.equation_14_verbatim_as_printed: Y_{i,t} = α + δ [POST_t × HIGH_UK_EXPOSURE_i] + θ CONTROLS_{i,t-1} + Σ_i FIRM_i + Σ_j Σ_t [INDUSTRY_j × QUARTER_t] + ε_{i,t}.    (14)
Q1_estimation_equation.verbatim_explanation_of_terms_page_3196_: The outcomes of interest, Y_{i,t}, are fixed capital investment, employment growth, R&D expenditures, divestitures, cash holdings, and NWC. HIGH_UK_EXPOSURE_i is a dummy variable that equals 1 if firm i is U.K.-exposed, and 0 otherwise. A firm is considered to be U.K.-exposed according to two measures: i) if it belongs to the top tercile of β_i^UK (market-based measure); or ii) if it has a high number of Brexit-related entries in its 2015 10-K form (textual-search-based measure). POST_t equals 1 if the time period is in the 2016:Q3-Q4 window.
Q1_estimation_equation.verbatim_controls_paragraph_page_3197: CONTROLS_{i,t-1} is a vector of macroeconomic and firm-level control variables. Macro controls include the lagged U.S. dollar/British pound FX rate, the lagged VIX implied volatility index, the lagged mean GDP growth 1-year-ahead forecast from the Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia's Livingstone Survey, the lagged Consumer Sentiment Index from the University of Michigan, and the lagged Leading Economic Indicator from the Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia. Firm-level controls include lagged stock returns, Tobin's Q, cash flow, logged assets, and sales growth. As an additional control for first-moment effects of Brexit, we add 1-quarter-ahead consensus earnings forecasts to our model. FIRM_i represents firm-fixed effects, INDUSTRY_j is a dummy for each industry category j of the Hoberg and Phillips (2016) classification (FIC 100), and QUARTER_t are calendar-quarter dummies. Standard errors are double-clustered by firm and calendar quarters.

interpretation_notes.lag_structure: The CONTROLS vector is indexed t-1, i.e. one-period lagged. Every variable the paper lists is explicitly described as 'lagged': lagged FX, lagged VIX, lagged GDP forecast, lagged Consumer Sentiment, lagged Leading Economic Indicator, lagged stock returns, and (by inheritance of the t-1 subscript) Tobin's Q, cash flow, logged assets, sales growth.
interpretation_notes.explicit_exception_to_lagging: The 1-quarter-AHEAD consensus earnings forecast is added as an additional control and is forward-looking, not lagged. Verbatim: 'As an additional control for first-moment effects of Brexit, we add 1-quarter-ahead consensus earnings forecasts to our model.'
interpretation_notes.dependent_variable_timing: Y_{i,t} is contemporaneous (subscript t, not t-1). The paper does not lag the dependent variable.
interpretation_notes.normalization_note_from_Table_1_notes_pa: Firm-level accounting variables are normalized by lagged total assets.

Q3_macroeconomic_controls_in_Table_8.Table_8_visual_inspection_finding: Table 8 (page 3208) does NOT print a 'Macroeconomic' row at all. The 'Controls' section contains only 'Firm.' Since 'Industry × time' is set to 'Yes' in all 6 Table 8 columns, the implied (but not stated) reason macro controls are omitted is collinearity with time fixed effects nested inside Industry × Quarter interactions.
Q3_macroeconomic_controls_in_Table_8.explicit_explanation_in_paper_text: The paper does NOT explicitly explain anywhere why macro controls drop when Industry × time FE is included. This is an econometric implication (macro variables vary only by t and are therefore absorbed by any set of fixed effects that includes Quarter-level variation), but it is left implicit. No verbatim sentence states 'we omit macro controls because they are absorbed by time FE.'

are_macro_controls_ever_included_with_In.answer_based_on_published_tables: Across all tables that report both rows (Table 2 explicitly, and by reference for tables that use equation (14)), the answer is no — Macro = Yes only when Industry × time = No, and vice versa. are_macro_controls_ever_included_with_In.caveat: The paper does not make a general statement that they are 'always mutually exclusive.' This is observed from table rows only.

are_additional_quarters_included.direct_answer: The paper does not explicitly state whether the regression sample is restricted to the 4 quarters (2015:Q3, 2015:Q4, 2016:Q3, 2016:Q4) or spans the broader panel (2010:Q1-2016:Q4) with POST=1 only on the last two quarters.
are_additional_quarters_included.indirect_evidence_for_broader_panel: Table 8 column 1 reports N=17,170 firm-quarter observations. With the tercile-based treatment scheme yielding 449+360=809 unique firms, a 4-quarter restriction would cap at ~3,236 observations. The 17,170 figure is consistent with a panel spanning ~21 quarters of usable data per firm, i.e. close to the full 2010:Q1-2016:Q4 estimation window with attrition. The DID identification then comes from POST being 1 only on 2016:Q3-Q4, while the firm and Industry×Quarter FE absorb level differences across firms and across industry-quarter cells.
are_additional_quarters_included.verbatim_quote_supporting_broad_sample_w: We use COMPUSTAT Quarterly to gather basic information on firm investment and financial data. We consider U.S. companies from the first calendar quarter of 2010 to the fourth quarter of 2016.
are_additional_quarters_included.verbatim_quote_supporting_end_of_window_: We limit our analysis to the end of 2016 due to the start of the Trump administration in Jan. 2017. We show in later robustness checks that results also hold for a window that excludes Trump's election.

why_these_quarters.verbatim_quote_page_3195_3196_on_window_: In our empirical tests, we compare two quarters before versus two quarters after the two key Brexit events we have just identified (Feb. 22 and June 23, 2016). We focus on a relatively short window around the Brexit vote as Bloom (2009) highlights the sharp yet short-lived nature of the economic effects triggered by uncertainty.

Q6_estimator.is_estimator_explicitly_named: No. The paper never writes 'OLS' or 'within estimator' or 'PanelOLS' or any specific estimator name in the main text describing the DID model.
what_paper_does_state: Equation (14) is presented as a linear regression with two-way (Firm; Industry×Quarter) fixed effects.
Standard errors are 'robust' and 'double-clustered by firm and calendar quarters.'
R^2 is reported in every table.
Q6_estimator.implied_estimator: Linear regression with the listed dummies (or, equivalently, within-transformation absorbing FIRM and INDUSTRY×QUARTER). The R^2 values reported (e.g. 0.21 for Table 8 col 1) are consistent with OLS-style R^2 on the demeaned or LSDV specification, but the paper does not state which.
what_paper_does_not_discuss: No mention of within-transformation versus LSDV.
No mention of degrees-of-freedom adjustments for the FE.
No mention of weighted vs. unweighted estimation.
No mention of software (e.g. Stata reghdfe, PanelOLS, etc.).

Q7_sample_for_Table_8.Table_8_column_1_observation_count: 17,170 firm-quarter observations (visually confirmed from Table 8 page 3208).
Q7_sample_for_Table_8.relationship_to_Supplementary_Table_C_1_: Table C.1 reports 41,630 firm-quarters as the final baseline sample BEFORE treatment selection. Table 8 col 1 (17,170) is smaller because it restricts to the top + bottom terciles of the nonnegative β_i^UK distribution (449 + 360 = 809 unique firms) and to firm-quarters where CASH and all controls are observed.
Q7_sample_for_Table_8.is_this_explicit_in_Table_8_notes: No. Table 8 notes do not cite 41,630 or N=17,170 explicitly. The notes only describe (i) the dependent variables, (ii) the treatment scheme, and (iii) the DiD time dimension.
Q7_sample_for_Table_8.verbatim_Table_8_notes_full_page_3208: Table 8 reports output from equation (14). The dependent variables are CASH, NON_CASH_WORKING_CAPITAL, and PROFITS. CASH is defined as total cash holdings divided by lagged total assets net of cash holdings. NON_CASH_WORKING_CAPITAL (NWC) is defined as working capital (net of cash) divided by lagged total assets. PROFITS is defined as the quarterly percentage change in profits (operating income before depreciation divided by sales). In the first specification, the treatment group is composed by the top tercile of β_i^UK, whereas the control group is composed by firms in the bottom tercile of β_i^UK. The second specification is a textual-search-based measure of U.K. exposure that sums up the number of Brexit-related words in firms' 2015 10-K forms. The treatment group is made of firms with more than five entries, whereas the control group are firms with zero entries. The time dimension of the DID estimator is set so as to compare the two quarters following the announcement of the referendum and Brexit's victory (2016:Q3-Q4) versus the two quarters preceding the announcement (2015:Q3-Q4). T-statistics are computed using robust standard errors (in parentheses) double-clustered at the firm and calendar quarter levels. *, **, and *** indicate statistical significance at the 10%, 5%, and 1% levels, respectively.
Q7_sample_for_Table_8.does_the_DiD_sample_include_all_quarters: Not explicitly stated in Table 8 notes or main text. See Q5 above for the indirect evidence pointing to the broader 2010:Q1-2016:Q4 panel as the regression sample, with POST identifying the 2016:Q3-Q4 quarters.
